name: Taj Mahal
description: An ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna river. Commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal. One of the Seven Wonders of the World and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Agra Fort
description: A grand 16th-century Mughal fort built from red sandstone on the banks of the Yamuna River. Served as the main residence of the emperors of the Mughal Dynasty until 1638. A UNESCO World Heritage Site with stunning courtyards and palaces.

name: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
description: The tomb of the Mughal Emperor Akbar, built in 1605–1613. It is an important Mughal architectural masterpiece located in the suburb of Sikandra.

name: Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
description: A Mughal mausoleum often described as a "jewel box", sometimes called the "Baby Taj". Built between 1622 and 1628, it represents a transition between the first phase of monumental Mughal architecture and its second phase.

name: Mehtab Bagh
description: A charbagh garden complex located north of the Taj Mahal complex and the Agra Fort on the opposite side of the Yamuna River, perfectly aligned with the Taj Mahal.

name: Anguri Bagh
description: A beautiful garden located inside the Agra Fort, known for its lush green lawns, stone pathways, and proximity to the Khas Mahal.

name: Jama Masjid Agra
description: One of the largest mosques in India, built by Shah Jahan in 1648 for his daughter Jahanara Begum. Located opposite the Agra Fort.

name: Bateshwar Temples Complex
description: An assembly of 101 beautiful white-painted Shiva temples lined up on the curved banks of the Yamuna River. Built by the Bhadauria dynasty kings, this quiet pilgrimage spot is also famous for its annual animal fair.

name: Mariam's Tomb
description: The mausoleum of Mariam-uz-Zamani, the Hindu wife of Mughal Emperor Akbar. Located in Sikandra, near Akbar's Tomb.

name: Chini Ka Rauza
description: A funerary monument containing the tomb of Allama Afzal Khan Mullah, a scholar and poet who was the Prime Minister of the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Famous for its glazed tile work.

name: AMU Jama Masjid
description: A grand 19th-century white marble mosque located inside the Aligarh Muslim University campus, showcasing beautiful minarets and arches.

name: Sir Syed House Museum (AMU)
description: A historic mansion housing personal belongings, letters, and rare photographs of AMU founder Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.

name: Aligarh Fort (Qila)
description: An ancient fort dating back to the 14th century, heavily fortified by French engineers and Marathas before being taken by the British. Houses a botanical garden and represents historic military designs.

name: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir
description: The grand Ram Mandir built at the birthplace of Lord Rama in the historic city of Ayodhya. A masterpiece of Nagara-style architecture, featuring hand-carved pink sandstone, five beautiful mandapas, and a high-sanctum shrine of Ram Lalla.

name: Hanumangarhi
description: A 10th-century temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman, situated on a hill. It is custom to visit Hanumangarhi before visiting the Ram Temple.

name: Gulab Bari
description: The tomb of Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula, surrounded by rose gardens. Features magnificent water fountains and impressive Nawabi architecture.

name: Katarniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A lush, forested Terai reserve that forms a vital wildlife corridor with Bardia National Park in Nepal. Celebrated for its population of gharials (crocodiles), gangetic dolphins, swamp deer, and tigers.

name: Kalinjar Fort
description: A fortress city in the Banda district of Bundelkhand. Situated on a rugged hill, this ancient fort was a stronghold of the Chandela dynasty. Features magnificent rock-cut sculptures, temples like Neelkanth, and historic gateways detailing battles of centuries past.

name: Bamaveshwar Temple
description: A hilltop temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, situated on the Bamaveshwar hill. Devotees climb several hundred steps for panoramic views.

name: Alakhnath Temple
description: One of the most famous Shiva temples in Bareilly, serving as the headquarters of the Anand Akhara sect of Naga Sannyasis.

name: Trivati Nath Temple
description: A historic temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, featuring a newly constructed multi-tiered gateway and beautiful carvings.

name: Samaspur Bird Sanctuary
description: A protected wetland sanctuary housing over 250 species of resident and migratory birds. Known for its quiet lakes, marshes, and tranquil birdwatching paths, it is a haven for nature lovers.

name: Bithoor Brahmavart Ghat
description: A historic town on the Ganges bank north of Kanpur. Brahmavart Ghat is believed to be the place where Lord Brahma created mankind. Also historically significant as the birthplace of Lakshmibai and center of the 1857 revolt under Nana Sahib.

name: Valmiki Ashram Bithoor
description: An ancient spiritual site where Sage Valmiki is said to have written the epic Ramayana. This peaceful ashram is also believed to be the place where Goddess Sita lived during her exile and gave birth to Lava and Kusha.

name: Kamadgiri Temple
description: A forested hill considered the heart of Chitrakoot, surrounded by temples. Devotees perform a 5km circumambulation (Parikrama) for blessings.

name: Chitrakoot Ramghat
description: A tranquil holy town on the Mandakini River banks. Ramghat is where Lord Rama, Goddess Sita, and Lakshmana are believed to have stayed during their exile and met poet Tulsidas. Known for peaceful evening riverboat aartis.

name: Hanuman Dhara
description: A hilltop shrine where a spring cascades down over a rock to touch the feet of a large Hanuman deity. Offers panoramic views of Chitrakoot.

name: Gupt Godavari Caves
description: A unique geological cavern system where a secret stream of water (Gupt Godavari) flows out of the rocks. According to legends, Lord Rama and Lakshmana held court inside these mysterious caves during their exile.

name: Sati Anusuya Ashram
description: A serene ashram nestled in thick forest, dedicated to Sage Atri and Sati Anusuya, marking the origin of the Mandakini River.

name: Sphatik Shila
description: A smooth rock structure featuring the footprints of Lord Rama and Goddess Sita, offering views of the Mandakini River below.

name: Fatehpur Sikri & Buland Darwaza
description: A historic fortified town founded in 1569 by Emperor Akbar, which served as the capital of the Mughal Empire. Famous for the Buland Darwaza, the highest gateway in the world, built to commemorate Akbar's victory over Gujarat.

name: Tomb of Salim Chishti
description: A spectacular white marble tomb located in the courtyard of Jama Masjid, built by Akbar to honor the Sufi saint Salim Chishti.

name: Panch Mahal
description: A unique five-story columnar pavilion built by Akbar, designed like a wind tower for cooling the palace interior. Offers panoramic views.

name: Marsalganj Jain Temple
description: A historic Jain pilgrimage site containing a miraculous 1000-year-old idol of Lord Rishabhdev, featuring detailed marble carvings.

name: Kalan Mosque
description: A medieval Tughlaq-era mosque built in the 14th century, showcasing unique dome architecture and arches, a hidden historic gem.

name: ISKCON Temple Ghaziabad
description: A beautiful temple and spiritual centre dedicated to Lord Krishna, featuring vibrant prayer halls, a vegetarian restaurant, and gardens.

name: Swarna Jayanti Park
description: A massive recreational park in Indirapuram featuring a boating lake, Japanese garden, jogging tracks, and musical fountains.

name: Tomb of Lord Cornwallis
description: The neoclassical mausoleum built in 1805 to honor Lord Cornwallis, the Governor-General of India, who died here. Built in white marble.

name: Ganga Bridge Ghazipur
description: A major structural landmark spanning the Ganges, offering scenic sunset and sunrise views of the river and local boatmen.

name: Geeta Press
description: The world's largest publisher of Hindu religious texts, founded in 1923. Houses a temple-like art gallery showcasing paintings of Lord Rama.

name: Gorakhnath Mandir
description: A grand, historically significant temple dedicated to Gorakhnath (a medieval saint of the Nath yogi sect). The temple and math complex serves as a major center of spiritual learning and hosts the Makar Sankranti Khichdi festival.

name: Ramgarh Tal Lake
description: A massive natural lake covering 1700 acres in Gorakhpur city. Recently beautified with walking corridors, a boating marina, water fountains, and a grand 30-meter high national flag, making it a favorite tourist hangout.

name: Veer Bahadur Singh Planetarium
description: An advanced three-dome astronomical observatory hosting educational shows about the solar system and stars for space enthusiasts.

name: Imambara Gorakhpur
description: A historic 18th-century structure known for keeping a continuous sacred flame (Dhuni) and housing gold and silver Tajias.

name: Jambudweep Jain Temple
description: A unique Jain pilgrimage temple representing Jain cosmology. Features a beautiful circular model of the mythological Jambudweep continent, including Mount Sumeru, rivers, and temples, situated in a green park.

name: Atala Masjid
description: A spectacular 15th-century mosque representing the Jaunpur style of architecture, built by Ibrahim Shah Sharqi. Features giant pylon gates.

name: Shahi Qila (Jaunpur Fort)
description: A 14th-century fort built by Feroz Shah Tughlaq on the banks of Gomti river. Known for its grand gate, mosque, and stone hammam.

name: Shahi Bridge (Akbari Bridge)
description: A grand 16th-century Mughal stone bridge spanning the Gomti River, featuring beautiful pillared kiosks for shops and views.

name: Jhansi Fort
description: A historic hilltop fortress built in the 17th century by Raja Bir Singh Deo. It is a symbol of courage and resistance, famously associated with Rani Lakshmibai (the Queen of Jhansi) who fought bravely against the British during the 1857 Rebellion.

name: Rani Mahal
description: The former palace of Rani Lakshmi Bai, displaying intricate carvings, colorful murals on the walls, and historical archaeological artifacts.

name: Cenotaph of Raja Gangadhar Rao
description: The commemorative monument built by Rani Lakshmi Bai in memory of her husband, located on the banks of Laxmi Tal.

name: Government Museum Jhansi
description: A museum highlighting the history of Jhansi, showcasing armory, terracotta sculptures, bronzes, manuscripts, and coins.

name: Barua Sagar
description: A scenic lake and historical fort site where a major battle was fought between the Marathas and the Bundelas. Famous for its historic ruins.

name: Gauri Shankar Temple
description: A historic temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, famous for its beautifully carved stone sculptures and ancient history dating back to King Harshavardhana.

name: Lakh Bahosi Bird Sanctuary
description: One of India's largest bird sanctuaries, spread over two lakes. Home to migratory waterbirds like storks, herons, and wild ducks.

name: Kannauj Archeological Museum
description: Houses a rare collection of ancient terracotta figurines, sculptures, and clay pottery dating back to the Kushan and Gupta periods.

name: JK Temple
description: A unique blend of ancient and modern architecture, built with white marble and featuring five shrines dedicated to different deities.

name: Allen Forest Zoo
description: One of the largest zoos in North India, spread over a lush forest area with natural habitats for tigers, leopards, rhinos, and birds.

name: Kanpur Memorial Church
description: A beautiful Gothic style church built in 1875 to honor the British soldiers who lost their lives in the Siege of Cawnpore in 1857.

name: Bhitargaon Gupta Brick Temple
description: An architectural treasure in Kanpur district. Built in the 5th century during the Gupta Empire, it is the oldest surviving terracota brick temple in India. A major landmark of ancient Indian temple design with refined brick moulding.

name: Moti Jheel
description: A scenic drinking-water reservoir transformed into a public recreational park, complete with boating, food stalls, and kids activity zones.

name: Phool Bagh
description: A historic park in the heart of Kanpur city, featuring a library, museum, and a majestic high-mast Indian national flag.

name: Kushinagar Mahaparinirvana Temple
description: The sacred place where Lord Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana (final salvation). The temple houses a magnificent 6-meter-long reclining red sandstone statue of Lord Buddha dating back to the Gupta era.

name: Ramabhar Stupa
description: The sacred mound marking the exact cremation site of Lord Buddha (Makutabandhana-Chaitya), situated near a scenic pond.

name: Wat Thai Temple Kushinagar
description: A beautiful monastery constructed in Thai style, featuring daily prayers, lush gardens, and a majestic golden Buddha statue.

name: Matha Kuar Shrine
description: An ancient temple housing a massive 10-foot-tall black stone statue of Buddha in the Bhumisparsha Mudra, dating back to 10th century.

name: Dudhwa National Park
description: A pristine forest reserve located in the Lakhimpur Kheri district, near the Nepal border. Spread over 490 sq km, it represents the semi-evergreen forests, wet grasslands, and swampy marshes of the Terai region. Home to tigers, leopards, one-horned rhinos, and swamp deer.

name: Frog Temple (Oel)
description: A unique, one-of-a-kind Shiva temple built in the shape of a giant frog, designed based on Tantric principles to resist floods.

name: Bara Imambara & Bhool Bhulaiya
description: An architectural marvel built by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula in 1784. Famous for its massive central hall built without any beams or pillars, and the intricate Bhool Bhulaiya (labyrinth) of corridors and terraces on the upper floor.

name: Chhota Imambara
description: An imposing monument built by Muhammad Ali Shah, the third Nawab of Awadh, in 1838. Known for its gorgeous chandeliers, gold-plated dome, and fine calligraphy.

name: Hazratganj
description: The downtown shopping district and cultural hub of Lucknow. Features Victorian-style buildings, cafes, theaters, and retail outlets.

name: State Museum Lucknow
description: Located in the Banarasi Bagh area, it houses a rich collection of archaeological findings, stone sculptures, coins, and paintings.

name: Dewa Sharif Shrine
description: The sacred tomb of Sufi Saint Haji Waris Ali Shah in Barabanki (near Lucknow). A unique symbol of universal brotherhood and Hindu-Muslim harmony. Known for the grand Dewa Mela and the saint's message of divine love: 'Love is the religion of all.'

name: Kakramath Temple
description: An ancient ruined Shiva temple located in the middle of a lake, featuring beautiful stone carvings reminiscent of Khajuraho temples.

name: Shiv Tandav Temple
description: A temple housing a rare, life-size granite idol of Lord Shiva in the dancing Tandav posture, carved during the Chandela dynasty.

name: Sun Temple Rahilya Ruins
description: A magnificent 9th-century granite stone temple dedicated to the Sun God, built by the Chandela dynasty kings on the Rahilya Sagar lake banks. It stands as a striking relic of early medieval architecture.

name: Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi
description: The highly revered temple complex built around the prison cell (Garbha Griha) where Lord Krishna is believed to have been born.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple
description: One of the oldest and largest temples in Mathura, famous for its magnificent architecture, carvings, and vibrant celebration of festivals.

name: Shri Radha Rani Temple
description: The royal temple dedicated to Radha Rani, situated on a hillock in Barsana. Reached by climbing a staircase of stone steps, the temple overlooks the historic town and is the epicenter of the famous Lathmar Holi festival.

name: Kusum Sarovar
description: A historic sandstone monument and a large water reservoir, surrounded by beautiful stairs and gardens, where Radha used to collect flowers.

name: Gita Mandir (Birla Mandir)
description: A beautiful marble temple dedicated to Lord Krishna, featuring the entire text of the Bhagavad Gita inscribed on its pillars.

name: Nand Bhawan Temple
description: The hilltop house of Nanda Baba in Nandgaon, offering panoramic views of the surrounding countryside. According to legends, Krishna's family moved here from Gokul to protect him from Kansa's demons.

name: Nanda Bhavan Gokul
description: The home of Nanda Baba, the foster father of Lord Krishna, in the pastoral town of Gokul. This structure is where Lord Krishna and Lord Balarama spent their childhood years under the care of Yashoda.

name: Vishram Ghat
description: The primary bathing ghat on the banks of Yamuna River where Lord Krishna rested after defeating the demon king Kansa.

name: St. John's Church
description: One of the oldest military churches in North India, built by the British East India Company in 1819 in the classical style.

name: Sardhana Basilica of Our Lady of Graces
description: A historic Catholic church built in 1822 by Begum Samru, the ruler of Sardhana. Designed by Italian architect Antonio Reghelini.

name: Chunar Fort Mirzapur
description: A historic fortress on a rocky spur overlooking the Ganges river, with history tracing back to 56 BC. Famous for its legends of King Vikramaditya, and Mughal emperor Humayun who fought battles here.

name: Windham Falls
description: A scenic waterfall surrounded by forests, perfect for family picnics and nature photography during the monsoon season.

name: Lakhaniya Dari Waterfalls
description: A hidden waterfall located amidst hills and forests, popular among trekkers for its scenic approach and natural pools.

name: Jama Masjid Moradabad
description: A grand historic mosque located on the banks of Ramganga river, built in 1631 by Rustam Khan, featuring beautiful domes and courtyard.

name: Prem Wonderland & Water Kingdom
description: A popular amusement and water park featuring thrill rides, swimming pools, and entertainment facilities for local families.

name: Buddh International Circuit
description: The premier motor racing circuit in India, located in Greater Noida. Hosted the Indian Formula One Grand Prix from 2011 to 2013.

name: Rashtriya Dalit Prerna Sthal
description: A massive memorial park on the Yamuna riverfront, featuring large sandstone pillars, elephant statues, and bronze busts of social reformers.

name: Botanic Garden of Indian Republic
description: A vast botanical conservation center containing endangered plant species, cactus houses, and medicinal gardens in the heart of Noida.

name: Okhla Bird Sanctuary
description: A protected wetland sanctuary situated at the entrance of Noida where the Yamuna River enters Uttar Pradesh. Home to over 300 bird species, especially migratory waterbirds. Perfect for morning nature walks.

name: Gauri Shankar Temple Pilibhit
description: A 250-year-old historic temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, situated on the banks of Devha river. Famous for its grand Shivratri celebrations.

name: Pilibhit Tiger Reserve
description: One of India's premier tiger reserves, located in the Pilibhit district along the India-Nepal border. Famous for its dense sal forests, rich water bodies, and successful tiger conservation efforts. A serene ecosystem perfect for birdwatching and wildlife safaris.

name: Bade Hanuman Temple
description: A unique temple near the Sangam featuring a large, reclining 20-foot idol of Lord Hanuman, which gets partially submerged during monsoons.

name: Triveni Sangam
description: The sacred confluence of the three holy rivers Ganges, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati. It is one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites in Hinduism and host to the historic Kumbh Mela, the largest peaceful gathering of humanity.

name: Chandra Shekhar Azad Park (Alfred Park)
description: The largest public park in Prayagraj, dedicated to the revolutionary leader Chandra Shekhar Azad who sacrificed his life here in 1931.

name: Rampur Raza Library
description: A world-renowned library housing a priceless collection of over 17,000 rare manuscripts, Mughal miniature paintings, and books.

name: Rampur Fort (Qila-e-Mualla)
description: The grand gateway and ruins of the historic fort built by Nawab Faizullah Khan, representing the heritage of Rampur state.

name: Sarnath Archaeological Museum
description: The oldest museum of the Archaeological Survey of India, housing the famous Lion Capital of Ashoka, which is India's national emblem.

name: Sarnath Dhamek Stupa
description: One of the most sacred Buddhist pilgrimage sites in the world. It is the place where Lord Gautama Buddha gave his first sermon to his five disciples after attaining enlightenment. Features the massive 43-meter high Dhamek Stupa.

name: Chaukhandi Stupa
description: An ancient Buddhist stupa built to mark the spot where Lord Buddha met his first five disciples. Features an octagonal tower built by Akbar.

name: Jetavana Monastery
description: An ancient monastery where Lord Gautama Buddha spent 24 monsoon seasons (rain retreats) and delivered many of his main discourses. The tranquil park contains ruins of monasteries, stupas, and the sacred Anandabodhi Tree.

name: Anathapindika's Stupa
description: The ruins of the historic stupa built by the wealthy merchant Anathapindika, who purchased Jetavana monastery using gold coins.

name: Angulimala's Stupa
description: The ruins of the ancient stupa built to commemorate the redemption of the notorious bandit Angulimala by Lord Buddha.

name: Salkhan Fossil Park
description: A unique geological heritage site containing petrified fossils of stromatolites dating back over 1.4 billion years, older than dinosaurs.

name: Mukha Falls
description: A scenic waterfall on the Belan River, cascading down steep rocky terrains. A beautiful picnic spot surrounded by wilderness.

name: Vijaygarh Fort
description: An ancient hilltop fort in the Sonbhadra district, featuring rock-cut caves, cave paintings, and water reservoirs that never dry up.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
description: One of the most famous Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is located in Varanasi, the holiest of Hindu cities, on the western bank of the holy river Ganges. Features a stunning gold-plated spire and a grand temple corridor.

name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
description: The main and most spectacular ghat in Varanasi, situated close to Vishwanath Temple. Famous for the Ganga Aarti, a daily spiritual ritual of fire and hymns conducted by young priests, creating a deeply spiritual ambiance.

name: Sarnath Dhamek Stupa
description: Located in Sarnath, just 10 km from Varanasi. This is the sacred park where Lord Gautama Buddha gave his first sermon to his disciples after attaining enlightenment. Features the massive 43-meter high Dhamek Stupa.

name: Assi Ghat
description: The southernmost ghat in Varanasi, situated at the confluence of the Ganges and Assi rivers. Highly famous for the Subah-e-Banaras morning ritual (yoga, classical music, and morning aarti), boat rides, and local cafes.

name: New Vishwanath Temple (BHU Birla Mandir)
description: A magnificent Shiva temple located inside the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) campus. Built by the Birla family, it features the tallest temple tower (Shikhara) in the world at 77 meters, made of pristine white marble.

name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
description: A sacred temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman, established by the legendary poet-saint Goswami Tulsidas in the early 16th century. Famous for hosting classical music festivals and being a spiritual sanctuary.

name: Manikarnika Ghat
description: The primary cremation ghat in Varanasi, reflecting the deep spiritual philosophy of life and death in Hinduism. It is believed that cremating a body here ensures Moksha (immediate liberation from the cycle of rebirth).

name: Scindia Ghat & Submerged Shiva Temple
description: A highly picturesque ghat famous for the Scindia Shiva Temple, which collapsed under its own weight during construction in 1830 and now stands partially submerged and tilted in the Ganges River.

name: Bharat Kala Bhavan Museum
description: A world-renowned art and archaeological museum located inside the BHU campus. Houses an extraordinary collection of miniature paintings, ancient clay sculptures, coins, and Buddhist relics.

name: Durga Temple (Monkey Temple)
description: An 18th-century temple built in the classical Nagara architectural style. Painted bright red, it features a multi-tiered spire and a sacred pond. Dedicated to Goddess Durga, it is home to many friendly monkeys.

name: Sri Kedar Temple & Kedar Ghat
description: One of the oldest temples in Varanasi, built in the distinct South Indian architectural style. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, the ghat and temple are popular among pilgrims from southern India.

name: Tulsi Manas Mandir
description: A modern white marble temple built in 1964. It is built at the exact location where Goswami Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas, the Hindi version of the Ramayana epic. The walls are beautifully engraved with verses from the epic.

name: Harishchandra Ghat
description: One of the two historic cremation ghats in Varanasi. Named after the legendary King Harishchandra who worked here to uphold truth and righteousness. Features modern eco-friendly cremation facilities.

name: Rajdari & Devdari Waterfalls
description: Stunning stepped waterfalls located inside the Chandra Prabha Wildlife Sanctuary (Chandauli, near Varanasi). A lush, forested getaway offering picnic spots, walking trails, and panoramic viewpoints over the green valley.

name: Lalita Ghat
description: A historic ghat named after Goddess Lalita Tripura Sundari. It houses the Nepali Temple and the Ganges-facing shrines. Highly popular for its artistic stone carvings and sunrise photography.

name: Raj Ghat
description: A peaceful and newly redeveloped ghat situated near the Malviya Bridge. Perfect for serene sunset views, birdwatching, and enjoying long walks away from the busy old city ghats.

name: Ramnagar Fort & Palace
description: An 18th-century sandstone fortress on the eastern bank of the Ganges River. Built by Kashi Naresh Raja Balwant Singh, it serves as the ancestral home of the Maharaja of Varanasi and houses a museum of royal collections.

name: Bharat Mata Mandir
description: A unique non-religious temple inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi in 1936. Instead of deities, it houses a large relief map of undivided India carved in flawless white marble, detailing mountain ranges, plains, and oceans.

name: Nepali Temple (Kathwala Mandir)
description: A beautiful temple constructed of wood, terracotta, and stone, built in the traditional Pagoda architecture of Nepal. Located at Lalita Ghat, it was built by the King of Nepal and features intricate woodwork.

name: Alamgir Mosque
description: A 17th-century mosque built by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb over the ruins of a grand Vishnu temple. Located majestically at the top of Panchganga Ghat, offering commanding views of the Ganges River.

name: Ashtabhuja Temple
description: A hilltop shrine dedicated to Goddess Ashtabhuja, sister of Lord Krishna, located in the Vindhyas. Famous for its cave temple layout.

name: Vindhyachal Vindhyavasini Temple
description: A highly revered Shakti Peeth temple dedicated to Goddess Vindhyavasini (Mahamaya). Located on the banks of River Ganges near Mirzapur, it is a spiritual hub attracting millions of devotees, particularly during Navratri.

name: Kali Khoh Temple
description: An ancient cave temple dedicated to Goddess Kali, situated at the base of the Vindhya range, surrounded by dense forests.

name: ISKCON Vrindavan
description: A major spiritual hub filled with constant chanting and devotional activities. Designed with exquisite white marble architecture.

name: Prem Mandir
description: A magnificent spiritual temple complex dedicated to divine love. Built entirely of pure white Italian Carrara marble, the temple features intricate carvings depicting the pastimes of Radha-Krishna and Ram-Sita. Illuminates beautifully at night.

name: Shri Banke Bihari Temple
description: One of the most sacred and popular temples in India dedicated to Lord Krishna. The black marble idol of Banke Bihari stands in a tribhanga (three-fold) posture, and the temple is famous for its vibrant Jhulan Yatra, Janmashtami, and Holi celebrations.

name: Radha Raman Temple
description: An ancient temple containing a self-manifested deity of Lord Krishna, self-emerged from a Saligram Shila, worshipped for over 500 years.

name: Radha Damodar Temple
description: An important temple established in 1542 by Srila Jiva Goswami, housing sacred deities and the footprint of Lord Krishna on a Govardhan Shila.

name: Sri Ranganatha Temple (Rangji Temple)
description: A grand temple showcasing a unique blend of South Indian (Dravidian) and North Indian architectural styles, dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

name: Nidhivan
description: A mysterious forest temple where the basil trees are believed to turn into Gopis at night for the celestial dance (Rasa Leela) of Krishna.

name: Katarmal Sun Temple
description: A unique 9th-century Sun temple displaying intricate wooden pillars and stone carvings.

name: Chitai Golu Devta
description: The highly revered temple of Golu Devta (god of justice), covered in thousands of brass bells and petition letters.

name: Kasar Devi Temple
description: A famous temple situated on a geomagnetic field ridge, popular for meditation since Swami Vivekananda's era.

name: Zero Point Binsar
description: A high watchtower inside Binsar Sanctuary, offering views of Kedarnath, Shivling, and Nanda Devi.

name: Crank's Ridge
description: Also known as Hippie Hill, famous as a counter-culture hub of Kasar Devi, offering valley views.

name: Gobind Ballabh Pant Museum
description: Exhibits ancient coins, Katyuri stone sculptures, tribal garments, and historical Kumaoni manuscripts.

name: Kalimut Viewpoint
description: A high scenic deck offering panoramic views of Almora town and the surrounding Kumaon hills.

name: Lakhudiyar Caves
description: Rock shelter caves containing prehistoric red and black finger paintings of dancing humans.

name: Jageshwar Dham
description: A cluster of 124 ancient stone temples built by Katyuri kings, nestled inside dense deodar forest.

name: Lala Bazaar Almora
description: A 200-year-old historic bazaar lined with stone-paved lanes and traditional carved wooden shopfronts.

name: Martola Picnic Spot
description: A scenic garden spot surrounded by oak and pine trees, popular for day travel.

name: Bright End Corner
description: A famous viewpoint in Almora offering beautiful sunset and sunrise views over Himalayas.

name: Deer Park Almora
description: A natural reserve forest park home to deer, leopards, and Himalayan black bears, featuring walking paths.

name: Nanda Devi Almora
description: A historic temple inside Almora town, dedicated to Goddess Nanda Devi, hosting the annual Nanda festival.

name: Simtola Eco Park
description: A pleasant municipal pine forest park offering children play slides and resting benches.

name: Chenab Lake
description: A small, quiet alpine lake reached by an adventurous forest trek, offering pristine nature.

name: Gurso Bugyal
description: A vast green alpine meadow offering panoramic views of Nanda Devi and Dronagiri peaks.

name: Auli Skiing School
description: The government training center for mountaineering and snow skiing courses.

name: Joshimath base viewpoint
description: A highway viewpoint offering sights of Joshimath town nestled on the hills below.

name: Nanda Devi view deck
description: A photography deck built by the tourism board for taking photos with Nanda Devi peak backdrop.

name: Auli Ropeway
description: Asia's longest ropeway cable car (4 km), connecting Joshimath to Auli ski slopes, offering valley views.

name: Auli Ski Slopes
description: World-class ski slopes situated between 2500m and 3000m, offering skiing lessons and snow peak views.

name: Saildhar Tapovan
description: A thermal hot spring area located near the river bed below Auli hills.

name: Trishul Peak Viewpoint
description: A scenic deck offering views of the triple peaks of Mount Trishul rising to 7120m.

name: Auli Sunset Point
description: A popular photography spot where the snow slopes reflect orange and purple sunset hues.

name: Chattrakund Lake
description: A small sweet water lake surrounded by dense pine forests, reached by a short meadow trek.

name: Auli Artificial Lake
description: One of the highest man-made lakes in the world, constructed to feed snow guns for the ski slopes.

name: Kwani Bugyal
description: A higher alpine meadow at 3384m, popular among trekkers and campers for summer views.

name: Auli Chair Lift
description: A chair lift ride connecting the lower ski resort to the upper artificial lake slopes.

name: Hanuman Temple Auli
description: A small local temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman, situated on the ski ridge.

name: Badrinath Temple
description: A premier Chardham temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu, featuring a colourful facade, situated at 3133m.

name: Narad Kund
description: A sacred pool in Alaknanda river where Adi Shankaracharya recovered the Badrinath idol.

name: Brahma Kapal
description: A flat riverbank platform where Hindus perform Shraddha rituals for ancestors.

name: Charanpaduka
description: A rocky meadow at 3380m featuring footprints believed to be of Lord Vishnu.

name: Mata Murti Temple
description: A temple dedicated to Badrinath's mother, situated on the banks of Alaknanda River.

name: Neelkanth Peak View
description: A viewpoint offering sights of the majestic Neelkanth Peak, known as the 'Garhwal Queen'.

name: Tapt Kund
description: Natural thermal hot sulfur springs located below Badrinath temple where pilgrims take holy baths.

name: Vasudhara Falls
description: A beautiful 400-foot waterfall cascading over rock cliffs, reached by a 5-km trek from Mana.

name: Vyas Gufa
description: An ancient cave in Mana where Sage Ved Vyas is believed to have composed the epic Mahabharata.

name: Mana Village
description: The last Indian village on the Indo-Tibetan border, famous for woolen carpets and potato farms.

name: Sheshnetra
description: A large boulder rock containing natural eye markings, believed to be the mythical serpent Sheshnag.

name: Bhim Pul
description: A natural giant stone bridge crossing the roaring Saraswati River, believed to have been placed by Bhima.

name: Alka Puri
description: The glacial basin from where Alaknanda River originates, offering peak views.

name: Saraswati River View
description: A river viewpoint showing the Saraswati River rushing out from glacial caves in Mana.

name: Ganesh Gufa
description: Another cave near Vyas Gufa where Lord Ganesha wrote down the epic dictation.

name: Bhimtal Lake Island
description: A scenic island inside Bhimtal lake, hosting a popular public aquarium.

name: Hidimba Parvat
description: A steep hill named after Hidimba of Mahabharata, offering trekking trails.

name: Butterfly Research Centre
description: A private museum housing a massive collection of exotic butterflies and forest insects.

name: Victoria Dam
description: A scenic terraced dam built in 1883 at one end of Bhimtal lake, featuring flower gardens.

name: Nal Damyanti Tal
description: A sacred small lake associated with the mythological stories of King Nala and Queen Damyanti.

name: Bhimtal Craft Market
description: Local bazaar stalls selling handmade wooden decorative toys and wool products.

name: Bhimtal Lake
description: A large natural lake in Bhimtal, larger than Nainital lake, featuring a central island.

name: Folk Culture Museum
description: Lok Sanskriti Sangrahalaya displays traditional Kumaoni paintings, manuscripts, and wooden models.

name: Bhimeshwar Mahadev Temple
description: An ancient Shiva temple situated on the lake embankment, built by King Baz Bahadur.

name: Karkotaka Temple
description: A hilltop temple dedicated to the mythical serpent god Karkotaka, offering valley views.

name: Binsar Photo Deck
description: A photography deck built by the tourism board for peak shots.

name: Khali Estate
description: A heritage bungalow estate where Mahatma Gandhi and Nehru stayed, now an eco-resort.

name: Binsar Sanctuary
description: A protected oak and rhododendron forest reserve, home to leopards and monal birds.

name: Zero Point Binsar
description: A high watchtower offering views of Himalayan peaks like Nanda Devi.

name: Binsar Forest Trail
description: An unpaved forest walking trail winding along deodar trees.

name: Binsar Sanctuary Museum
description: An educational center displaying wildlife skulls, forest maps, and details of local flora.

name: Gairad Golu Devta
description: A popular local temple of Golu Devta, decorated with bells and letters.

name: Kasar Devi Temple view
